name: Finbar
soft_passes: #2 fin anchors lower-right third, not optical grid centre — acceptable for a scene icon but not glyph-centred, and contributes to the 16px failure
failures: #3 silhouette — filled solid the art collapses to a plain squircle; fin/waves read only via internal colour, never outline; not nameable from shape alone
#4 16px squint — menu rows vanish, fin degrades to an unidentifiable green smudge, reads as a generic gray-blue glass blob (recovers by 32px)
#7 figure-ground — fin-vs-panel luminance contrast 1.02:1 (floor 3:1); whole icon is a low-contrast value mush, hierarchy by hue + thin rim-lights only; grayscale confirms fin nearly disappears
#10 variant robustness — baked raster (specular/glow painted in), not layered Icon Composer; identity depends on light-gray panel + specific blue/mint; would not survive dark/clear/tinted renders
light_model: top-down / frontal glass, single consistent source; baked soft specular along panel top, pill tops, wave crests and fin leading edge; short soft shadows; cyan rim-light on the fin
layer_stack: frosted gray glass panel (menu/search window field)
abstracted UI rows + top search-field pill (the 'bar')
devices: Finbar double-pun: shark 'fin' + menu-rows/search-pill 'bar' — name rendered as image
waterline doubles as a selected-list-row band (one shape, two readings)
the app's own search panel used as the icon's background field
rim-lit translucent glass fin with refraction-style inner gradient
rhymes_hint: frosted Liquid-Glass scene-diorama icons; 'app-UI-as-icon' window-motif family (icon depicts a stylized version of the app's own panel); pun-driven marine/mascot indie icons with a literal-subject anchor
notes: Clean native 1024x1024 PNG, transparent corners, no upscaling artifacts — genuine source, not a resized web render. Mask handled correctly (art bleeds under squircle). Specular/glow/shadow are BAKED (HIG says let the system apply these) — this is a raster emulation of Liquid Glass, not authored Icon Composer layers, so system dark/clear/tinted variants won't exist. It is genuinely a scene/diorama; glyph_type='object' marks the fin as the intended anchor but the scene construction is why #3/#4/#7 fail. Cover coherence: icon abstracts the app's real gray menu list + system-blue selected row into frosted panel + blue water + teal band; icon-to-app palette coheres on blue, mint/teal fin is icon-only brand flavour. For synthesis: candidate clusters 'app-UI-as-icon window-motif' and 'frosted glass scene-diorama'; flag a 'low-contrast value-mush / hierarchy-by-hue-only' anti-pattern to watch if more glassy scene icons arrive. Strong subject-mining, weak Dock-size legibility — the two findings that matter.
